data.turoyo: Əmmi: “Ṭayyəb, iḏa d əmmat l u=alohayḏux: aḥna d matərkina i=ḥaramtiyaṯi w u=salb w u=tanhibano, aḥna, aloho gədxofər ḥṭiṯayḏan?” Omər: “Ahla w sahla gdomanne.”
data.translation: Sie sagten: "Gut, wirst du wohl zu deinem Gott sagen: Wenn wir dieses Räuberbandwerk und das ausrauben und ausplündern aufgeben, wird Gott dann wohl unsere Sünde verzeihen?" Er sprach: "Ich werde es ihm gerne sagen."

rationale: Fills Infectum sense 1; gəd- prospective forgiveness in the first petition, distinct from the inherited repeated petition at /79.

summary: All three tokens fit I.1 verzeihen with God as actor and sin as the zero-marked affected object. The sinners are represented as possessors of sin, not as a separately expressed recipient.

The two Infectum petitions ask about prospective forgiveness after abandoning robbery; Preterit xfəlle presents forgiveness as already accomplished when the intention is uttered. The temporal coincidence is a discourse/aspect observation, not a separate performative sense.
The Preterit has l aloho as overt L-marked actor corresponding to -le. Compare unmarked aloho in the Infectum petitions; this contrast is grammatical actor coding, not a divine recipient.
Preserve x in gədxofər, gxofər and xfəlle. The current entry already files x-spellings under ġfr and separately has ġofar in Ilyas p.c.; the three tokens do not establish a new root.
No idiom or additional sense is proposed. The current entry already cites /79 correctly; no citation correction is warranted.
Is ġ/x variation phonetic, dialectal or editorial in these sources? The spellings are preserved without normalizing one to the other.
Does speaker usage distinguish the possibility/prospective force of the two petition forms, or is the difference only gəd- versus g- in context?
